Rooftop solar adoption among Goan households: evidence from a survey

Abstract

We study rooftop solar adoption using a survey of 1,204 households in North Goa and South Goa. Adoption is higher among households with a member working abroad. We discuss implications for subsidy design.

Keywords: rooftop solar, adoption, remittances, Goa

1. Introduction

Rooftop solar has spread slowly in Goa despite generous subsidies. Previous work on India has focused on large states (Shrimali and Jindal, 2019; Kumar, 2021). We add evidence from a small coastal state, where remittances from the Gulf are an important source of household income.

2. Data

The survey was carried out between June and September 2023 by trained enumerators. It covered 1,204 households in 48 villages and 6 towns. The response rate was 81 per cent. We use a logit model with village fixed effects; standard errors are clustered by village.

3. Results

Households with a member abroad are 9 percentage points more likely to have installed rooftop solar (95% CI: 4 to 14). The effect is larger in South Goa. Roof ownership matters more than income: tenants almost never adopt.
